newsitem.title: USA: NAPM report shows manufacturing slowed in October.
newsitem.headline: NAPM report shows manufacturing slowed in October.

text.p: The U.S. manufacturing sector grew more slowly in October than in September, according to a survey of the nation's purchasing executives released Friday.

The National Association of Purchasing Management said its monthly index fell to 50.2 percent in October from 51.7 percent in September. A reading above 50 indicates the manufacturing economy is generally expanding, while one below that indicates contraction.

"Purchasing executives' comments on business conditions in October included more remarks such as 'slowing' and 'orders down' than those indicating 'business good' or 'strong,'" said Ralph Kauffman, chair of the group's business survey committee.
The NAPM surveys more than 300 purchasing executives monthly to obtain their assessment of the economy.
The group cited declines in reported new orders, order backlogs, inventories and employment for the drop in the overall index.
